desks.Dividends: Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 per quarter (pay Dec 10), is the only declared watchlist ex-date in the window, its 24th consecutive annual increase, and the last purchase day for entitlement is Wed Nov 18. The $0.98 has been public since Sep 15, so no information edge attaches to the ex-date itself. Apple's dividend is still undeclared; a mid-November date is pattern-plausible but UNVERIFIED until declared, and a declaration could accompany its Nov 2 earnings, so re-check before Monday's open. Nvidia's next declaration normally accompanies its Nov 17 earnings, pointing to an early-December ex-date outside the window. SPY and QQQ point to mid-December on pattern only, Tesla pays no dividend, and no cuts or specials were found.
desks.Earnings: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close (call 5:00 p.m. ET) with an options-implied move of about 4.2% to 4.3% from the Nov 4 straddle, against a reported typical move of about 2% over the past eight quarters; consensus is UNVERIFIED as a single figure, with sources citing $1.99 and $2.02 EPS and about $113.4 billion and $115.5 billion revenue. Microsoft reported Oct 28 and Tesla reported Oct 21. Nvidia reports Tue Nov 17 after close, just outside this window, with its implied move UNVERIFIED as a single figure (about 8.7% against about 5.1% across sources).
desks.Futures: Brent December settled Fri Oct 30 at $117.64 and January at $113.43, with WTI at $104.12; the $4.21 Brent gap is the December-to-January roll, not a selloff. OPEC+ held December targets unchanged Sun Nov 1 against an estimated 4.2 million barrel-per-day actual-output shortfall. US December gas fell 3% to $2.858 per MMBtu, with the March-April 2027 spread at a record low of about 5 cents and the calendar-2027 strip at a 58-month low, against European gas above 100 euros per megawatt-hour. Grains await the Nov 10 WASDE at 12:00 p.m. ET, with corn 60% and soybeans 79% harvested. Next catalysts in order: midterms Tue Nov 3, EIA gas Thu Nov 5, WASDE Tue Nov 10, EIA petroleum Thu Nov 12, OPEC+ Sun Nov 29.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist. The S&P Dow Jones style-index methodology overhaul, with pro-forma files Dec 4 and effective before the open Dec 21, changes growth/value classification, not S&P 500 membership, and matters for style-ETF rebalancing flow around Dec 4-21, not for parity math. A cited estimate puts at least $375 billion in passive funds tied to the affected gauges, attributed and not desk-verified. A preprint on SPX and RUT parity residuals describes a funding and capital wedge, not a visible arbitrage failure, which supports the standing rule that parity math wins over a screen or model.
desks.Premium: Apple's Nov 4 expiry at 51.7% implied volatility live, against 14.9% trailing realized volatility, is event pricing ahead of the Nov 2 print, not a mispricing signal, and premium into the binary is to be avoided; the Nov 6 expiry sits at 47.3%. SPY has no clean implied-versus-realized verdict: Friday's move drives 32.2% of the fresh 20-day window's variance, over the 30% line, so the read is WINDOW-CONTINGENT, and QQQ sits just under the line at 29.8%. Live implied volatilities run above the Oct 31 file prints on all six names, but markets were closed all weekend, so that gap is two vintages of the same Friday session disagreeing, not a weekend jump, and its cause is UNVERIFIED. Front-expiry call-put implied volatility gaps are wide for SPY and QQQ on weekend-stale quotes and are flagged, not claimed as violations. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names.
desks.Quant lab: Four new candidates were appended to the ledger as rows 197-200, with no TEST and no INTEGRATE movement this run. The strongest is the earnings-disclosure study using optimal transport to separate repeated from novel content in press releases and call Q&A (score 59, WATCH), valued as a reading lens for what in the call is genuinely new, not as a tradable signal. Second is the frozen-evidence evaluation study for AI equity agents (score 54, WATCH), valued for its versioned-database and dependency-graph discipline for purged walk-forward work. The GitHub new-repo discovery leg was skipped this run, so arXiv and dataset legs carried the sweep.

headline: Daily research brief — Sunday, November 1

items.detail: Apple reports Mon Nov 2 after close, with the Nov 4 expiry straddle implying a move of about 4.2% to 4.3%, against a reported typical move of about 2% over the past eight quarters on a next-close basis. That straddle runs to Nov 4, so it includes movement beyond the single post-earnings session; the earnings-only stripped figure is about 3.0%. Front implied volatility of 51.7% sits above the Nov 6 expiry at 47.3%, the earnings hump. The December-quarter guide is the swing factor, not the September print, with the Jul 30 precedent in mind: a beat that still closed down 7.4%.
items.title: Apple reports Monday after close, and premium into the print is event pricing

items.detail: Friday closes put SPY at $755.72, down 1.77%, QQQ at $690.49, down 3.47%, and Nvidia at $204.64, down 4.22%. Friday's move drives 32.23% of the fresh 20-day SPY variance window, over the 30% line, so any SPY implied-versus-realized read is WINDOW-CONTINGENT; an independent recomputation from daily closes puts the share at about 30.8%, which also clears the line, so the marking stands. QQQ at 29.79% sits just under the line and is one heavy day from tripping it. All quotes here are Friday-close marks, not live Sunday prints.
items.title: SPY has no clean volatility verdict after Friday's selloff

items.detail: Brent's expiring December contract settled Fri Oct 30 at $117.64, against $113.43 for January, a $4.21 prompt premium consistent with near-term disruption pricing. OPEC+ agreed Sun Nov 1 to hold December targets unchanged, against an estimated actual-output shortfall of about 4.2 million barrels per day, so quotas are not the binding constraint; tanker movement through Hormuz is. Hormuz physical flow volumes are UNVERIFIED in free sources: two narratives, about 70% below baseline and near pre-war levels via a shuttle lane, are unreconciled. US December gas fell 3% to $2.858 per MMBtu, with the March-April 2027 spread at a record low of about 5 cents.
items.title: Crude carries a prompt Hormuz premium; US gas prices the opposite story

items.detail: FRED prints dated Thu Oct 29, the latest in the pull, put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.61% and the 10-year at 4.98%, a 2s10s spread of +37 basis points after widening 5 points over the week. SOFR at 3.94% sits 6 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. Near 5%, the 10-year remains a valuation headwind for long-duration names on discount-rate grounds, not a volatility signal. Friday Oct 30 FRED observations had not yet landed at run time.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.98%, curve sloping up, funding calm
